skill.displayName: Workplace Group Stress Heatmap | 职场员工压力群体热力图

llm.summary: This skill is a sensitive workplace camera-analysis tool that sends media to a cloud API and keeps persistent user/report identity state despite presenting the analysis as anonymous.

dimensions.detail: Uploading workplace camera videos or URLs and retrieving cloud-stored historical reports is high-impact for employee privacy; consent guidance exists, but the automatic cloud and identity flows are broader than a simple local anonymous heatmap tool.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package is a Python skill with bundled scripts, shared helper modules, YAML config, and dependencies such as requests, SQLAlchemy, pydash, and PyYAML; I found no remote code retrieval, shell persistence installer, or obfuscated execution path.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill auto-triggers on office camera video and historical-report keywords, requires cloud report lookup for report lists, and instructs the agent not to ask for or expose internal identity parameters, which reduces user visibility over a sensitive surveillance workflow.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The common utilities read a workspace data/smyx-api-key.txt value, create or reuse a persistent default open_id, register/login through a backend, and store tokens/open tokens and profile fields in a workspace SQLite database for reuse.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is group-level anonymous workplace stress heatmaps from office camera footage, but runtime behavior delegates media analysis and historical report access to a remote LifeEmergence API; the artifact does not provide auditable local enforcement of its anonymity and minimum-sample guarantees.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this before installing in any real workplace. It may upload office camera footage or video URLs to an external service, silently associate activity with a persistent internal user/report identity, and retrieve cloud-stored historical reports. Only use it with clear employee notice, consent, retention limits, access controls, and confidence that the external service enforces the promised anonymous group-level processing.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The generic API-client implementation is partly expected for a cloud-backed analysis skill, so I did not treat the lack of local computer-vision code as malicious by itself; it remains a concern because the claimed privacy controls are not locally verifiable.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The artifact claims anonymous, non-identifying employee analysis while also requiring silent internal identity association for users and reports; this is not employee face identification, but it is under-disclosed identity linkage for a sensitive workflow.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The skill includes consent and compliance notes, but the overall workflow processes workplace camera footage for stress inference and cloud reporting, which warrants stronger front-loaded warning and administrative controls.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Persistent open_id creation/reuse and cloud historical report association are documented as internal automatic behavior, but they materially weaken the simple anonymity framing.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The inspected code confirms hidden --open-id/--api-key parameters, default open_id generation/reuse, backend silent registration/login, and local token/profile storage in SQLite.
[LP3] expected: Network calls, local file reads for uploaded videos, and output writes are normal for this API-backed skill; the least-privilege concern is mainly that the skill lacks a clear permission boundary for sensitive media and cloud report access.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Automatic triggering for historical report queries and broad office-camera analysis requests can expose sensitive past workplace-monitoring results without an explicit confirmation step.
